source.place: Kerodon, Example 3.1.8.10, Path Fibrations (tag 0101), together with Remark 3.4.0.6, Homotopy Fibers (tag 0328); online source, archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Put $I=\Delta^1$. An $n$-simplex of $E_f$ is a pair $(x,\gamma)$ with $x:\Delta^n\to P$ and $\gamma:I\times\Delta^n\to Q$ satisfying $\gamma(0,z)=f(x(z))$. Define $r(x,\gamma)=x$, $p(x,\gamma)(z)=\gamma(1,z)$, and $i(x)=(x,\gamma_x)$ where $\gamma_x(s,z)=f(x(z))$. These formulas commute with all simplicial operators, and give $ri=\mathrm{id}_P$ and $pi=f$.

source.place: Example 3.1.8.10: the path object and the factorization; formulas expanded degreewise.

proof.text: Let $\partial I\subseteq I$ be the simplicial subset of constant maps $[m]\to[1]$, i.e. the two vertices $\{0\}\amalg\{1\}$; the inclusion is degreewise injective. Since $Q$ is Kan, $Q\to\Delta^0$ lifts every horn inclusion. Apply [lem-cbc-internal-hom-fibration-corner-map] to $\partial I\hookrightarrow I$ and $Q\to\Delta^0$. Both functor simplicial sets into $\Delta^0$ are $\Delta^0$, so the corner target is $\operatorname{Fun}(\partial I,Q)$; as $\partial I\times\Delta^n$ is two disjoint copies of $\Delta^n$, $\operatorname{Fun}(\partial I,Q)_n=Q_n\times Q_n$ compatibly with all operators, and the restriction map becomes the endpoint map $e=(\operatorname{ev}_0,\operatorname{ev}_1):\operatorname{Fun}(I,Q)\to Q\times Q$. Hence $e$ is a Kan fibration. Concretely, a horn $\Lambda_k^n\to\operatorname{Fun}(I,Q)$ together with a simplex $\Delta^n\to Q\times Q$ agreeing with its endpoints on $\Lambda_k^n$ extends to $\Delta^n\to\operatorname{Fun}(I,Q)$ with exactly those endpoints. Applying it with endpoint pair $(fx,b)$ gives the required path extension in Step 3.

source.place: Corollary 3.1.3.3 specialized to the monomorphism ∂Δ^1↪Δ^1, as used in Example 3.1.8.10 (0101), second bullet.

proof.text: To lift a horn against $p$, write the given horn in $E_f$ as $(x_\Lambda,\gamma_\Lambda)$ and the given simplex in $Q$ as $b:\Delta^n\to Q$, with $\gamma_\Lambda(1,-)=b|_{\Lambda_k^n}$. Since $P$ is Kan, extend $x_\Lambda$ to $x:\Delta^n\to P$. Step 2 applied to the horn $\gamma_\Lambda$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(I,Q)$ and the endpoint pair $(fx,b)$ extends it to $\gamma$ with endpoints exactly $(fx,b)$. Then $(x,\gamma)$ is the required lift against $p$. Thus $p$ is a Kan fibration. In particular $E_f$ is Kan: fill the projection of any horn into $Q$ first and then lift that filler against $p$.

source.place: Example 3.1.8.10, second bullet; base change and composition of fibrations written as the two successive horn lifts.

proof.text: There is an explicit simplicial homotopy $H:E_f\times I\to E_f$ from $ir$ to $\mathrm{id}_{E_f}$. On an $n$-simplex $((x,\gamma),t)$, where $t:\Delta^n\to I$, set $H((x,\gamma),t)=(x,\gamma_t)$ with $\gamma_t(s,z)=\gamma(\min(s,t(z)),z)$. Here $\min:I\times I\to I$ is the simplicial map induced by the order-preserving map $\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}\to\{0,1\}$ taking the minimum; explicitly on simplices it is pointwise minimum of two monotone maps. Thus it commutes with precomposition by every simplex operator. Because $\min(0,t)=0$, the initial endpoint remains $fx$, so $H$ takes values in $E_f$. At $t=0$ it is $ir$, and at $t=1$ it is the identity.

source.place: Example 3.1.8.10, first bullet: elementary explicit contraction replacing the trivial-fibration argument; agent expansion.

proof.text: For every small Kan complex $W$, precomposition with $i$ and $r$ gives maps $i^*:\operatorname{Fun}(E_f,W)\to\operatorname{Fun}(P,W)$ and $r^*$ in the opposite direction. They induce inverse maps on edge components: $i^*r^*=\mathrm{id}$ follows from $ri=\mathrm{id}$, and for each vertex $a:E_f\to W$, the map $aH:E_f\times I\to W$ is an edge from $a\circ i\circ r$ to $a$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(E_f,W)$ (interchange the two product factors in the definition of $\operatorname{Fun}$). Hence $r^*i^*$ induces the identity on these components. The cited Kan-target testing criterion, applied to $v=i$, now proves that $|i|$ induces the required bijection on path components and isomorphisms on all based homotopy groups. This is precisely the weak homotopy equivalence convention of the item.

source.place: Corollary 3.6.4.3 and Definition 3.1.7.12 (00UA); application of the existing realization/Kan-target criterion to the explicit homotopy.

proof.text: Finally fix a vertex $q$ of $Q$. Degreewise, the strict fiber of $p$ consists of the pairs $(x,\gamma)$ of Step 1 with $\gamma(1,z)=q$ for every $z$. Its simplicial operators restrict those pairs. It is therefore exactly $P\times_{Q,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,Q)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,Q}\{q\}$, the specified definition of the homotopy fiber. It is Kan: for a horn in this fiber, lift against $p$ using the constant simplex at $q$ as its prescribed projection. This proves the fiber clause without any comparison between ordinary fibers and homotopy fibers beyond the displayed equality.

source.place: Remark 3.4.0.6, strict fibers of the path fibration; equality with the homotopy-fiber formula of the definition node.

proof_origin.place: Paragraph 2, mapping-space foundations of the coherent finite coefficient adjunction. Online Kerodon 0101 supplies the path-fibration route; explicit contraction and horn arguments are agent expansions because the online source is not archived.

title: Path-space replacement computes homotopy fibers
statement: Use spaces, horns, functor simplicial sets $\operatorname{Fun}(K,-)$ with evaluation maps, weak homotopy equivalences and homotopy fibers as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A Kan fibration is a simplicial map with the right lifting property against every horn inclusion $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ with $n\geq1$ and $0\leq i\leq n$ (outer horns included). For a map of small Kan complexes $f:P\to Q$, form the path-space object $E_f=P\times_{Q,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,Q)$ and let $p:E_f\to Q$ be induced by $\operatorname{ev}_1$. Then $p$ is a Kan fibration, the inclusion of $P$ by constant paths is a weak homotopy equivalence $i:P\to E_f$ with $p\circ i=f$, and for each vertex $q\in Q$ the strict fiber $\{q\}\times_Q E_f$ is the homotopy fiber of $f$ over $q$ as defined in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].
